If you're still on the fence about installing macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple's massive batch of security fixes might be enough to convince you. If you choose to stay on an older version, you should install macOS Tahoe 26.7 or macOS Sequoia 15.7 as soon as possible. Here's why.

Apple fixes 200+ macOS vulnerabilities

Apple today published the full security release notes for macOS 27 Golden Gate, macOS Tahoe 26.7, and macOS Sequoia 15.8, detailing the more than 200 vulnerabilities addressed in this round of updates.

As with several recent macOS updates, Apple's acknowledgements list includes multiple AI-focused security teams and researchers, including OpenAI Codex Security, NVIDIA AI Red Team, and Anthropic Research.

The fixes included in macOS 27 cover a wide range of vulnerabilities that could allow malicious apps or attackers to execute arbitrary code with kernel or root privileges, escape the macOS sandbox, bypass Gatekeeper protections, modify protected system files, access sensitive user data, and much more.

For example, an AVEVideoEncoder vulnerability could allow a sandboxed app to execute arbitrary code with kernel privileges. Meanwhile, a UDF file system vulnerability could similarly allow apps to execute code at the kernel level. Apple also fixed vulnerabilities that could lead to remote code execution via Bluetooth, CUPS, and WebDAV.

As for macOS Tahoe 26.7 and macOS Sequoia 15.8, both updates patch many of the same vulnerabilities mentioned above, including several at the kernel level, root privileges, sandbox escapes, Gatekeeper bypasses, and remote code execution.

The older versions also include some additional fixes not listed in macOS 27, including an ImageIO vulnerability in macOS Sequoia 15.8 that could lead to arbitrary code execution when processing a specially crafted malicious image.
